integrity: Every squarefree-semiprime solution is reduced bijectively to a divisor d<=k of k^2+1. The attached exact checker tests all such divisors for every 1<=k<=132, verifies primality by trial division and rechecks the original hyperperfect identity. The classical divisor criterion and the finite certificate together establish the claimed cutoff.
scientific_limitations: The claim concerns only squarefree semiprimes pq and does not compare multiplicities across all hyperperfect factorization types. The divisor factorization (p-k)(q-k)=k^2+1 is classical; the new claim is the exhaustive first multiplicity-three cutoff. The 1984 source predates the exact metadata date but its inspected record supplies only a publication year, so the date field uses the earliest exact public calendar day verified among the inspected archival sources.
title: First triple squarefree-semiprime hyperperfect index
